gameplay_summary: Ninja action platformer: as Ryu Hayabusa, framed for the death of agent Irene Lew by a double, climb, wall-cling and slash through stages including new vertical-scrolling sections, with an item that extends sword reach.

Mechanical enemies are more common, vertical-scrolling stages are introduced, the shadow-clone technique of II is gone, and a new item extends the sword's reach. gameplay_summary: Party dungeon crawl: lead adventurers across a wilderness with six cities and many dungeons to recover the seven pieces of the shattered Destiny Wand, defeat the archmage Lagoth Zanta and reforge the wand.
dossier: Pony Canyon's Famicom version of Interplay's 1986 Bard's Tale II, the last designed by Michael Cranford. It expands the first game's single city into a wider world with an explorable wilderness, six cities and many dungeons, and adds casinos and banks. Your party seeks the seven pieces of the broken Destiny Wand, held in dungeons such as the Tombs, Fanskar's Fortress, Dargoth's Castle and the Maze of Dread, while mercenaries roam the land. Defeating the archmage Lagoth Zanta and reforging the wand makes its wielder the immortal Destiny Knight. An optional starter dungeon in Tangramayne helps build fledgling characters. gameplay_summary: Shogi study software supervised by the Japan Shogi Association: replay historic professional games in commentary or watch modes, stepping manually or automatically.
dossier: Hect's second Shogi Meikan, supervised by the Japan Shogi Association and released on 30 January 1992. Like the first, it's a collection of past professional games rather than a game against the computer. You watch them in commentary or spectator modes, either automatically or move by move, across five categories each holding many games.
